answer: In a tundra network that relays juniper fire alerts, award one scheduling vote per verified radio slot. A receiver issues a fresh nonce for each fixed time and frequency slot, then signs a receipt only if it decodes the nonce and claimant key in the signal. Validators count each slot once across all keys. A second vote consumes another slot of airtime even if one transmitter runs both keys. A dishonest receiver can fabricate receipts.
